instruction: I'm interested in the NVIDIA research team behind this paper. Please find and bookmark the personal webpages of all authors affiliated with NVIDIA, and organize them in a folder called 'Liked Authors' under the 'Bookmarks bar'.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-20)

metadata.explanation: Task targets all authors with NVIDIA affiliation (superscript 1): Linxi Fan, Ajay Mandlekar, De-An Huang, Yuke Zhu, and Anima Anandkumar. Expected URLs based on NVIDIA research profiles and typical academic webpages. Uses existing bookmark evaluator.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction ambiguity: 'personal webpages' is unclear - does not specify whether to bookmark ONE URL per author or ALL URLs per author

Overly restrictive matching logic: The metric uses itertools.product() to generate all possible combinations of URLs (one per author) and only passes if exactly ONE URL from each author's list is bookmarked, matching one of ~243 possible combinations

Fails for comprehensive bookmarking: If a user bookmarks ALL URLs for all authors (19 total URLs - a reasonable interpretation of 'bookmark the personal webpages'), the metric will FAIL because set comparison expects exactly 5 URLs

Semantic inconsistency: The instruction says 'personal webpages' (typically academic/personal sites) but the expected URLs include LinkedIn profiles, and the metric treats all URL types equally, allowing ONLY LinkedIn profiles to pass
No partial credit: The metric is all-or-nothing - bookmarking 4 out of 5 authors correctly returns 0.0, not reflecting partial task completion

URL selection logic unclear: Why accept LinkedIn as equivalent to personal webpage? The expected URL alternatives per author mix different types of webpages (personal sites, institutional profiles, social media) without clear priority
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Clarify instruction: Specify 'bookmark ONE personal webpage for each author' to remove ambiguity

Fix metric logic: Instead of using product() combinations, check that (1) folder exists, (2) contains at least one URL from each author's list, and (3) all bookmarked URLs belong to the expected authors
Add partial credit: Return score as (number of authors with at least one URL bookmarked) / 5.0
Prioritize URL types: If 'personal webpages' means academic/personal sites, the expected URLs should prioritize those (jimfan.me, yukezhu.me, tensorlab.cms.caltech.edu) over LinkedIn profiles
Alternative approach: Use a more flexible matching that checks if each of the 5 authors has at least one of their URLs bookmarked in the 'Liked Authors' folder, regardless of total bookmark count
